The '''2018–19 Danish Superliga''' season was the 29th season of the [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Danish Superliga|Superliga]]. [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]] were the defending champions. The season started on 13 July 2018 and ended on 26 May 2019.

==Teams==
[[FC Helsingør]] finished as loser in the relegation play-offs in the [[2017–18 Danish Superliga|2017–18 season]] and was relegated to the [[2018–19 Danish 1st Division|2018–19 1st Division]] along with [[Silkeborg IF]], and [[Lyngby BK|Lyngby]] who lost their respective relegation play-offs as well.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2017–18 Danish 1st Division|2017–18 1st Division]] champions [[Vejle BK]], who returned after nine years of absence, as well as the play-off winners [[Vendsyssel FF]] who got promoted to the top division for the first time ever, and  [[Esbjerg fB]] who returned after a one-year absence.

==European play-offs==
The winning team from the 4-team knock-out tournament will advance to a Europa League play-off match. In the final, the team with the most points from the relegation round group stage will host the second leg.

If the [[2018–19 Danish Cup]] winner, found on 17 May in the [[2019 Danish Cup Final|final]], is involved in the play-offs, they will be withdrawn, as they will enter the Europa League third qualifying round directly.

==Relegation play-offs==
The relegation play-offs were streamlined slightly compared to the [[2017–18 Danish Superliga#Relegation play-offs|previous system]], essentially doing away with the former first round.
{{#invoke:RoundN|N8

|Match 2 (12 and 19 May 2019)|[[Hobro IK|Hobro]] |0|2|[[Vejle Boldklub|Vejle]]|1|0

|Match 3 (30 May and 2 June 2019)|[[Lyngby Boldklub|Lyngby]]|2|2 |[[Vendsyssel FF|Vendsyssel]]|1|2 
|Match 4 (30 May and 2 June 2019)|[[Hobro IK|Hobro]]|1|2 |[[Viborg FF|Viborg]]|0|0 
}}

The winner of match 1 finished 11th and stayed in the Superliga, while the losers of match 2 finished 14th and were relegated directly.
